other_failure_modes.name: Destruction of categorical features
other_failure_modes.description: Using pd.to_numeric with errors='coerce' on categorical string columns converts all valid string values to NaN. This effectively destroys all categorical features instead of properly encoding them for the model.

other_failure_modes.name: Test set data leakage during imputation
other_failure_modes.description: The test set's missing values are imputed using the test set's own median rather than the training set's median. This causes data leakage and makes the pipeline incapable of correctly predicting on a single new instance.

other_failure_modes.name: Imputation before cross-validation split
other_failure_modes.description: Missing values in the training set are imputed using the median of the entire training set before the K-Fold cross-validation split, leaking validation fold statistics into the training folds.

other_failure_modes.name: Using only the last fold's model for test predictions
other_failure_modes.description: In cross-validation, the model variable is reassigned in each fold. Predicting on the test set outside the loop uses only the model trained on the final fold, discarding the ensemble of models.

summary: The agent implements a basic LightGBM pipeline with 5-fold cross-validation but makes several critical errors in data preprocessing. Applying pd.to_numeric with 'coerce' to object columns destroys all categorical string data by turning it into NaNs. Furthermore, imputing the test set with its own median introduces data leakage, and test predictions are incorrectly made using only the model from the final cross-validation fold.
